missions.title: A damaged display item
paragraphs: A shop has only one desk lamp left. The display lamp has a visible scratch. The issue calls for a judgement about the relevant constraint and the effect of leaving it unresolved.

The recommendation is to ask about its condition and any available alternative. The expected benefit is that the customer can decide with complete information. The rationale should be explained to any stakeholder whose work or plans depend on the outcome.

The relevant stakeholder should be able to identify the immediate action, the assumption supporting it, and the condition that would justify reconsideration. Accountability includes checking whether the expected benefit actually materialises.

Within the agreed scope, the team can name a contact for follow-up questions. The expected benefit is that the colleague can get clarification when needed. The rationale should be explained to any stakeholder whose work or plans depend on the outcome.

The action should be assessed against the purpose of the task and the needs of the people affected. A defensible decision remains open to revision when a material assumption changes. Documenting the reasoning creates a basis for learning and reduces the risk of repeating a process whose usefulness has not been established.

missions.title: An unfinished task list
paragraphs: An employee prepares for a week away. Several tasks are only recorded in personal notes. The issue calls for a judgement about the relevant constraint and the effect of leaving it unresolved.

Pending confirmation of the details, the team plans to share a list of unfinished tasks and their next steps. The expected benefit is that other team members can continue the work. The rationale should be explained to any stakeholder whose work or plans depend on the outcome.

The team should make the scope of its commitment clear and avoid transferring an unresolved dependency to someone who cannot control it. A proportionate review can test whether the response worked under the actual conditions. Any adjustment should follow from the evidence rather than from a wish to defend the original plan.

missions.title: A handover with old information
paragraphs: A handover document includes last month's procedure. The procedure changed earlier this week. The issue calls for a judgement about the relevant constraint and the effect of leaving it unresolved.

A defensible recommendation is to replace the outdated instructions before sharing. The expected benefit is that the next person can follow the current process. The rationale should be explained to any stakeholder whose work or plans depend on the outcome.

The decision provides a basis for coordinated action, but its adequacy still requires evaluation. A relevant stakeholder should understand the expected benefit, the outstanding uncertainty, and the next point for review. That distinction between agreement and verified effectiveness is central to reliable professional communication.
